name: île de la Cité
locality: 1st arrondissement of Paris, 4th arrondissement of Paris
text: The Île de la Cité (French: [il d(ə) la site]; lit. "Island of the City") is one of two natural islands on the Seine River (alongside Île Saint-Louis) in central Paris. It spans 22.5 hectares (56 acres) of land.

depictions.name: Ile de la Cite
depictions.text: The Île de la Cité is one of two remaining natural islands on the Seine within the city of Paris. During the 18th century, it was one of Paris' seven major districts, consisting of the Palais de Justice, Cité, and Île Saint-Louis sub-districts. One major landmark on the island was the Notre-Dame cathedral, a large Gothic-style church that took over one hundred years to complete.
